rule: a round of its own: it holds the hidden rows its own looks revealed and scores computed against the hidden rows (play.computed_against_hidden_rows); ask for it apart from a person's round on the same episode, or after it

episode.rule: the first 12 overpasses at or after the requested start with a detection in the box
episode.chosen_from: MODIS rows only (VIIRS is hidden and was dropped before choosing)
episode.looks_note: one slot per pass of a hidden platform whose swath holds the whole box, from NASA CMR granule metadata: the time the scan crossed the box and the pixel size there, both from the swath polygon. Nothing is read from the hidden rows. A pass with no hidden detection is scored as a look that flagged nothing; VIIRS granules carry no cloud information and MODIS cloud cover is a granule mean, so such a look may have been cloudy.
episode.reward: the score after the look minus the score before it, on one fixed set: every real hidden detection of the episode. The rewards of a round add up to the score at the end minus the score at the start. A look that hands over no hidden pixel earns nothing.

taught_elsewhere.on: the cells outside every tile looked at, at the look it was looked at

play.tile_scores_are: the player's own score for each tile at a look it decides; null for a player that does not rank tiles
play.known_limits: FIRMS lists detections, not where a satellite looked and saw nothing, and has no cloud mask: a revealed tile with no detection may have been cloudy rather than free of fire. So a look that hands over no detection is taken as unknown: it teaches the model nothing and earns nothing. The looks are the passes of each VIIRS platform whose swath held the whole box, from NASA's pass list, at their real times and pixel sizes; a pass that held only part of the box is not a look.
